title: 2027-11-01 - Redwood discovery: model selection with Lotus AI
summary: Initial discovery to understand Lotus AI's model selection needs across hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Focus on long-context multilingual retrieval, tool-calling, and open model comparisons. Action items include benchmark dataset share, security doc packet, and schedule a technical deep dive and pilot pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Send tailored pricing for dedicated pilot and hosted comparison
Share security packet (SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS docs)
Run 2-week benchmark with Lotus sample dataset (Redwood to provision)
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (Diego + Lotus platform)
action_items: Diego Alvarez: Prepare benchmark run plan and list of required sample data (due: 2027-11-05)
Maya Chen: Send pricing and pilot options + Redwood deck link (due: 2027-11-03)
Priya Nair: Share representative dataset and example prompts (due: 2027-11-04)
Maya Chen: Share SOC2 and KMS integration docs (due: 2027-11-03)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Diego (SE) is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya (Lotus): Hi, thanks—yeah doing well. Aisha's on in a bit, but we can start. We wanted to focus on model selection for some of our new products—long context, multi-lingual, and we need tool calling for retrieval and internal APIs.
[00:20] Diego (SE): Great. Quick agenda—context length needs, model accuracy across languages, tool-calling/function-calls, and infra options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. We'll also touch on benchmarks and security. Does that sound right?
[00:31] Tom (Lotus): Yep that's it. We're leaning towards open models because of cost and control but want Redwood's take on which open models are practical for production.
[00:40] Maya: Awesome. Can you share a bit about scale—qps, avg tokens per request, and peak concurrency?
[00:48] Priya: We're prototyping at the moment. Typical request is a retrieval-augmented generation flow with a 30k token context—combining doc store + convo history. Expected to ramp to ~20 qps for some endpoints, and peaks maybe 60 qps. Latency target is sub-500ms for user facing but ok to have async for heavy jobs.
[01:05] Diego: 30k tokens, noted. So context length is a major factor. For open models, we usually compare Llama-4x-like families (the community variants), Mistral mix, Falcon-40B, and some of the optimized LLMs that support extended context with saving KV cache. There's a tradeoff: models that support 32k natively vs chunking with retrieval.
[01:25] Priya: Right. We're also multilingual—Hindi, Arabic, English, and some East Asian languages. We need to know which models degrade and whether to use translation layer.
[01:34] Diego: Mistral-style models do well on many European languages; Llama derivatives have broader community fine-tunes for multilingual. Falcon sometimes struggles on lower-resource languages. We can run side-by-side evals on your dataset; we normally surface ROUGE/EM and more subjective evals for generation quality per locale.
[01:50] Aisha (CTO) (joined): Sorry for the delay. Quick question on infra—we have sensitive PII in some docs. Likely need VPC plus customer-managed KMS, is that supported?
[01:59] Maya: Yes—Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and full VPC peering or on-prem options. Dedicated also supports KMS + isolated GPU pools but control plane is managed. Hosted keeps logs for 30 days by default but we can discuss retention and enterprise packages.
[02:15] Tom: On cost—if we go 30k contexts at 20 qps, is dedicated required? We want predictable throughput but don't want to overcommit.
[02:24] Diego: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale; Hosted is easier to start and we can run a Hosted pilot, then reserve Dedicated for sustained load. There's also autoscale burst for Dedicated to handle peaks.
[02:37] Priya: Tool-calling—we need ability to call internal APIs for structured data insertion, and also a retriever that can pass embedding ids. Does Redwood support function calling or tool APIs?
[02:45] Diego: We support function/tool calling patterns in the API—structured outputs, tool hooks. For retrieval, caching the KV cache and prefix caching is important for repeated contexts to reduce latency/cost.
[02:56] Priya: Good. Also, do you support quantized models for lower cost? We often consider int8/int4 quantization.
[03:03] Diego: Yes, our runtime supports quantized execution paths and we recommend model-specific quant profiles. We can recommend quantization strategies depending on quality tradeoffs—often int8 works well for many open models; int4 can be aggressive but sometimes acceptable for embeddings.
[03:18] Maya: On the security side, what attestations do you have? SOC2 Type II, ISO?
[03:23] Maya (AE): I can share our security packet—SOC2, ISO is in progress, SSO via SAML/OIDC supported, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. We'll share links in the follow-up.
[03:36] Tom: Are there known latency numbers for, say, Falcon-40b vs a Llama-variant on a 32k context in Redwood Hosted?
[03:44] Diego: Latency depends on kernel optimizations, sequence length distribution, and hardware. Roughly, on a dedicated GPU with optimized kernels Falcon can be slightly faster for dense decoding, but Mistral and quantized Llama-forks often win on cost/quality. We have benchmark sheets—we'll run your dataset to give apples-to-apples numbers.
[04:01] Priya: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[04:06] Diego: Sample documents, representative prompts, and a small holdout eval set. Also indicate languages and retrieval patterns. We'll provision a 2-week benchmark with Hosted test instances and show token cost, latency p50/p95, and generation quality per model.
[04:19] Aisha: On data residency—some data must remain in EU regions. Does Redwood have region pinning for Private/Dedicated?
[04:26] Maya: Yes—region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports regional endpoints in our cloud regions, and for strict residency Private on-prem is the option.
[04:35] Tom: Any gotchas around function calling with long contexts? We worry about extraneous tokens and cost when you pass 30k tokens.
[04:43] Diego: We advise hybrid approach: retrieval + summarization to reduce context, prefix caching for stable portions, and chunking large docs into embeddings so you only pass relevant snippets. That reduces both latency and cost.
[04:56] Priya: Sounds good. Can you share examples of customers who use long-context RAG with Redwood?
[05:02] Maya: Yes—we have a couple of enterprise references in similar domains; we'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[05:10] Tom: What are typical SLOs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:15] Diego: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets per contract. Hosted has strong availability but no guaranteed SLA on free tiers—enterprise Hosted customers can get higher SLAs and retention.
[05:26] Priya: Ok—let's recap next steps.
[05:30] Maya: We'll: 1) send tailored pricing + Redwood deck link, 2) share SOC2/KMS/SSO docs, 3) Diego will prepare benchmark plan and list of data we need, 4) schedule a technical deep dive next week. Anything else?
[05:44] Aisha: Please include cost estimates for quantized vs non-quantized models and a rough estimate for Dedicated commit sizes.
[05:51] Maya: Noted. We'll follow up with those numbers and a proposed pilot timeline.
[05:56] Priya: Great, thanks everyone.
[05:58] Maya: Thanks, bye.
[06:00] (call ended)
